summary.headline: Gem Aromatics Q1 FY27 standalone revenue rose to INR83 crore (from INR76 crore) but consolidated EBITDA fell to INR3.3 crore (3.3% margin) and consolidated PAT was a INR7.9 crore loss.
summary.overview: Standalone revenue grew about 9% YoY to INR83 crore, with consolidated revenue at INR99 crore versus INR88 crore, helped by a seasonally soft Q1. Margins compressed on product mix, clove raw-material costs after Madagascar floods, and a higher fixed cost base at the new Dahej plant. Consolidated PAT was a loss of INR7.9 crore, pressured by INR9.1 crore of higher depreciation after capitalisation of most of the INR270 crore Dahej capex. Management says the new verticals (cooling agents, Safranal/Citral, phenol derivatives) start contributing from Q2 to Q4 FY27, with FY27 framed as a ramp-up year and no guidance given.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR76 crore in Q1 FY26 (about +9% YoY)
vs INR88 crore in Q1 FY26 (about +12% YoY)
Higher depreciation of INR9.1 crore after Dahej capitalisation

segments.name: Gem (core: clove and mint)
segments.commentary: Clove volumes and sales were hit by Madagascar cyclone/floods, with Toamasina port shut for close to 30 days; incoming raw material resumed from May. Mint harvest runs May to July, with export orders now flowing, though some May-June shipments were not yet recognised as they had not reached destinations.

segments.name: Krystal Ingredients (Dahej, wholly owned subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Safranal commercial production has started, with revenue expected by end-Q2 FY27 and meaningful from Q3. Cooling agents Gemcool 3, 5 and 23 are in production with initial orders; meaningful contribution expected from Q3 FY27. Phenol derivatives: trial production by end-Q2, commercial production targeted Q3, meaningful revenue from Q4 FY27.

guidance_outlook: No FY27 revenue or margin guidance; management will give guidance toward calendar year-end for the next year.
Krystal products expected to exceed 50% of overall revenue in FY28.
Management expects Eugenol and derivatives to be fairly close to planned numbers by year-end FY27, per Yash Parekh.
Cooling agents: management expects a large part of the targeted volumes (on 500-ton capacity, about 25% utilisation with two customers) to show up in Q3 and Q4.
Operating leverage expected to support margins and profitability over the medium term as utilisation rises.
capex_capacity: Total Dahej plant capex about INR270 crore; nearly INR265 crore incurred and substantially capitalised.
Standby capacity at Dahej is already absorbing depreciation, interest and manpower costs ahead of revenue.
Cooling agents: 500-ton capacity referenced by analyst; management said utilisation would be close to the analyst's 25% figure.
Phenol derivatives: commercial production targeted Q3 FY27, subject to approvals and quality processes.
Brazil subsidiary approved to expand Latin America distribution for essential oils, aroma chemicals and specialty chemicals.
demand_pricing: Management says demand is back to normal levels, with Western Hemisphere (US and Latin America) demand ramping up.
Cooling agents are used in oral care, confectionery and specialty flavours; cooling agent approvals from two of the world's largest consumers, per management.
Clove raw-material pricing rose after Madagascar supply disruption, weighing on margins.
Shipping challenges out of India and to the Western Hemisphere are a key concern for timing.
Currency: management said the rupee depreciation is neither a tactical advantage nor disadvantage, since imports are hedged.

qa_highlights.question: Where is demand coming from in the core business, and which geographies are growing?
qa_highlights.answer: Demand is back to normal; Western Hemisphere (US and Latin America) is ramping, with export deal flow and new product seasonality expected to show in Q2 and Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Is the phenol derivatives ramp delayed, and what is the timeline to commercial production?
qa_highlights.answer: Trial production by end-Q2 FY27, commercial production in Q3, meaningful revenue from Q4 FY27; pilot batches are approved and customers want plant-level trials. Traders and distributors are being targeted for faster approvals.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Madagascar disruption materially delay the Eugenol ramp, and is clove tree supply structurally at risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Port reopened and material is flowing; management expects Eugenol numbers close to plan by year-end. Trees are still productive and sourcing is diversified across Madagascar and East Africa, so no major structural issue foreseen.

qa_highlights.question: How will the business reach sustainable consolidated profitability?
qa_highlights.answer: Management blamed a timing mismatch: depreciation, interest and manpower costs are already in the P&L while higher-margin Krystal revenue has not yet arrived. Profitability should improve as the new products ramp.

qa_highlights.question: How will working capital evolve for Krystal?
qa_highlights.answer: Krystal is synthetic and needs less inventory, so its working cycle should be lower than Gem's; factoring is also being used to reduce debtor days.

qa_highlights.question: Can you quantify the Gemcool orders, and are new products higher margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Order values and customer names are not being disclosed. Management said each new product is intended to be more margin-accretive than existing products; several are in approval stages with revenue expected from Q3 and Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Did the tariff-relief restocking show up in Q1 FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Mint harvest timing, clove delays and shipping issues pushed revenue into later periods; May-June exports were made but not yet recognised as they had not reached final destinations, with roll-over expected in July-August.

risks_watch: Consolidated loss and 3.3% EBITDA margin until Krystal revenue ramps; depreciation of INR9.1 crore per quarter will persist.
Qualification timelines for cooling agents, Safranal and phenol derivatives; any slippage from Q2/Q3/Q4 FY27 targets.
Clove supply from Madagascar and shipping disruptions to the Western Hemisphere.
Clove and raw-material cost pass-through, given higher clove costs in Q1.
Working capital and cash generation at the consolidated level; standalone cash PAT (INR8.9 crore) compares with consolidated cash PAT of INR1.3 crore.
Customer and order disclosure is limited; no order values or customer names given.
summary.management_tone: Confident on long-term commercialisation and the Krystal pipeline, but cautious and evasive on near-term numbers: no FY27 guidance, no order values, and no margin ballpark. Near-term weakness is attributed to Madagascar, shipping, mix and the timing of new-plant costs.
key_quotes: So, the demand remains as strong and back to normal levels.
And for cooling agents, for example, we've already been approved by the world's two largest companies who are consuming that product.
So, FY '27, you know, is, you know, more like a ramp-up year where, you know, one by one we'll be starting off each vertical.
So, the working capital cycle for Krystal should be much lower than, the Gem business currently.

So, the whole idea is to keep continue, it's a multipurpose plant, there are value-added products that we have made in terms of our entire capacity and they are -- we've started producing those products, they are in different stages of approvals.
